headline: Roughly half of US children who have Tourette syndrome have never been formally diagnosed — the diagnosed pool is the market today, but a large latent, under-identified population sits behind it.

stats.label: of children with TS are undiagnosed

funnel.title: Diagnosed-patient funnel (illustrative; each stage cited)
funnel.note: Directional funnel from all US children to the drug-eligible pool. Stage rates are literature-anchored, not claims-derived. Treatment-warranting share reflects the moderate-to-severe / impairing minority per AAN.

stages.label: Reach a tic-treating specialist
stages.note: diagnostic + referral bottleneck; ~4 clinicians consulted before dx

comorbidity.title: TS is rarely isolated — comorbidity drives who owns the patient
comorbidity.note: ~86% of children with TS have >=1 psychiatric comorbidity; only ~10-15% have 'pure' TS. ADHD/OCD/anxiety often pull the patient toward child psychiatry / developmental-behavioral pediatrics, while the tic disorder pulls toward pediatric neurology.

regional_caveat: Published region-by-region TS prevalence is thin; do NOT assert a raw regional biology gradient. Defensible framing: DIAGNOSED prevalence concentrates around specialist access and the Center-of-Excellence footprint (see Channel & Sites).
